title: Low vitamin B-12 concentrations in patients without anemia: the effect of folic acid fortification of grain
authors: Mills JL, Von Kohorn I, Conley MR, Zeller JA, Cox C, Williamson RE, et al.
followUp: Laboratory records 1992 to 2000, before, during optional and after mandatory fortification
population: Every patient with a serum vitamin B12 below 258 pmol/L at the Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Washington DC
funder: Supported by the intramural research program at the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, NIH, DHHS.
result: Of 1573 patients with low B12, the proportion without anaemia was 39.2% before fortification, 45.5% during optional fortification and 37.6% after mandatory fortification, without a significant increase; unchanged when restricted to patients over 60 years or to B12 below 150 pmol/L. Neurological outcomes were not assessed. The authors state that, if confirmed, fortification has not caused a major increase in masking of B12 deficiency.
